title: K-PWM: Control-Oriented Structured Bilinear World Models under Partial Observation
claim: An unknown real system is mirrored by a learned structured latent model that lifts states, evolves them bilinearly under actions, and decodes observations.
layout: 2 stacked dashed panels, left-to-right flow, red lifting arrow linking world and latent
description: The figure has two stacked dashed rounded boxes. The top magenta box, "World evolution (unknown)", shows the true state chain x_{k-1} → F_d → x_k, driven by action a_{k-1}. State x_k passes through a diamond g, then a sum with noise ν_k, to give the grey observed y_k. The bottom blue box, "Latent evolution (K-PWM)", shows z_{k-1} → a yellow "Koopman bilinear transition" block (Σ a_i G_i) → sum with noise w_k → z_k. abstract: World models learn internal simulators of environment dynamics for prediction, planning, and control, yet learning them from limited, noisy, and partial observations remains challenging. While much progress has focused on pixel-based observations, many physical systems instead provide vector-valued measurements that reveal only part of the underlying state. We introduce K-PWM, a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation. K-PWM couples Koopman-bilinear latent dynamics with a nonlinear observation decoder and performs probabilistic latent-state inference through the learned model via extended Kalman filtering and smoothing, without a separately trained inference network. Its bilinear structure enables exact propagation of the maintained Gaussian belief through the latent transition and efficient rollouts for uncertainty-aware model predictive path integral (MPPI) control. For training K-PWM, we present a generalized expectation conditional maximization (GECM) procedure with closed-form updates for the generators, noise covariances, and latent prior, complemented by gradient-based decoder learning. A Koopman-consistent initialization selects the latent dimension from data and initializes the action-dependent dynamics. With limited training data, K-PWM achieves lower long-horizon prediction error than the evaluated baselines on partially observed Gymnasium MuJoCo systems, while substantially reducing training time relative to the strongest prediction baseline. On high-dimensional MuJoCo Menagerie robots, it achieves competitive tracking accuracy with low per-step computation times, demonstrating potential for real-time deployment. These results support structured probabilistic dynamics as a data- and compute-efficient approach to world modeling and control under partial observation.
